one_month_reasoning: No Micron earnings before 1 Nov (FQ1 FY27 report mid/late Dec). In the window: (1) Taiwan labour dispute: Taoyuan strike-authorization vote in early Oct, Micron's revised bonus framework due for board approval in early Oct, Taichung mediation 22 Oct [17,18,19,20]. As of 5 Oct no vote result is published; authorization is likely (80%+ backed action in August) but an actual walkout is less likely, so it is a negative-skew headline rather than a supply event; a concession toward a permanent 15%-of-operating-profit pool would weigh on FY27-28 EPS sentiment. (2) Samsung Q3 prelim (early Oct), SK hynix Q3 (27/28 Oct), Kioxia (~30 Oct), FOMC 27-28 Oct, hyperscaler capex guides late Oct: read-through on HBM/AI demand, which I expect neutral-to-supportive given TrendForce's 4Q26 contract increases [3]. (3) My lane's pricing trackers show spot plateauing: DDR5 die +3.7% 30d with weekly gains slowing, DDR4 16Gb 'early cooling signal' [4], DDR4 2Gx8 correcting and NAND wafer spot -1% w/w with 'no clear buying interest' [16]. Spot usually leads contract by a quarter or two, so this is a mild negative for sentiment within the month even though contract prices are still rising. Net: near-symmetric lognormal around spot at ~20% monthly sigma (slightly below 80%/3.5 since realized vol is inflated by the one-way run) with a small negative tilt for the strike headline and the spot plateau; P(>=spot) 0.465.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) FY28 EPS $198 x 5.1x = $1,010 and (b) normalized EPS $108 x 9.5x = $1,026 plus ~$170/sh horizon net cash = $1,196; blended $1,103, ~2.5% above spot.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Aug-28) EPS $198 x 5.1x forward P/E (value in Oct 2027 when FY28 is the NTM year)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 consensus $205.95 [11] cut ~4% (was 5%). The supervisor showed consensus is more likely to rise after the FQ1 guide came in ~8% above consensus [1,21], so I narrowed the haircut; I keep a small one because my lane's spot trackers show the price impulse fading (DDR5 spot +3.7% 30d and slowing, DDR4 2Gx8 correcting, NAND wafer spot falling [4,16]) and TrendForce's 4Q26 contract rises are a deceleration [3].

Core DRAM/NAND peers on one NTM basis: SK hynix ~4.65x, Samsung ~4.73x, Nanya ~5.4x, Kioxia ~4.2x, Sandisk ~7.8x, median ~4.7x [12,21]. 5.1x is ~8% above the median: persistent support from the SCA floor (~$150B RPO at minimum prices, >35% of revenue to 2030) and the Korea/Taiwan listing discount [2]; Samsung's own large net cash means I give no extra for the balance sheet. Below MU's current ~6.0x NTM because by Oct 2027 the market will be pricing the 2028 supply wave.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Through-cycle EPS $108 x 9.5x = $1,026, plus projected net cash ~$170/share at Oct 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus GM path declines from ~84% to ~65% by FY2030 [10]; ~$250B revenue (below FY27 consensus $274.9B [11]) at ~55% operating margin and 15.5% tax [2] gives ~$116B NI / 1.15B diluted shares [1] = ~$101 (was /1.13B); nudged to $108 for the SCA floor ('margins meaningfully above any prior cycle peak') [2]. Prior-cycle collapse from low-60s GM to 27% [7] is the cautionary history.

Core memory peers trade ~4.7x NTM on earnings roughly double through-cycle levels [12,21], equivalent to ~9-10x normalized; memory names traded ~10-13x forward at mid-cycle [7]. 9.5x sits at the low end of that.

Net cash $68.3B less $12.7B refundable SCA deposits = $55.6B [1,2]; FY27 FCF ~ consensus NI ~$203B ($176.42 x 1.15B [11]) + ~$12B D&A (FY26 $9.5B [1]) - capex ~$55B (>$50B, FQ1 $11.5B [2]) - ~$10B working capital/tax timing = ~$150B; total ~$205B / 1.15B = ~$178, trimmed to $170 for execution risk. Buybacks are value-neutral (they shrink shares), correcting my round-1 error of deducting them [21].

bear.story: Spot weakness already visible in NAND and DDR4 [16] spreads to DDR5 in 1H27; consumer demand destruction plus an HBM price reset; supply from SK hynix Y1 (Feb-27), Samsung P5 (1H27), Micron ID1 and Tongluo (mid-27) and CXMT lets investors look through 2027; Taiwan labour settles at a permanent profit pool. FY28 EPS cut to ~$140 at ~3x plus ~$150/sh cash.

base.story: FY27 ~$180-190 EPS with sequential growth as guided; pricing moderates but stays tight into 2028; labour dispute settles with higher but bounded bonuses; market pays ~5.1x FY28 EPS ~$198 (~$1,010) and gives some credit for ~$170/sh cash and capital return from Dec 2026.

bull.story: Shortage deepens in 2027-28 (2027 HBM ASP +121% [3], NewMaxx-style conventional DRAM scarcity [6]); SCAs/RPO convince investors earnings are durable; FY28 EPS ~$230 and the multiple holds ~6.5x plus cash.

MU ~6.0x NTM P/E, ~4.6x NTM EV/EBITDA. Only five genuine DRAM/NAND manufacturers are listed; round 1's HDD (WDC, STX), controller (SIMO, Phison) and NOR/SLC specialists (Winbond, Macronix) are dropped as different technology/supply structures, and my round-1 'EV/EBITDA median 13.95x' was trailing, mislabelled as forward.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Small premium only, on two persistent factors: SCA contracts covering >35% of revenue through 2030 with floor prices (~$150B RPO) [2] and the Korea/Taiwan listing discount. I dropped the net-cash/payout argument from round 1 because Samsung also holds very large net cash (supervisor finding). Peers also hold long-term HBM contracts, so I cap the premium below 10%. No sell-side outperformance call used.

thesis_break_reason: Rebuilt from post-print numbers: with ~$170/sh of horizon net cash, $660 puts the ex-cash value at ~$490, i.e. ~2.5x FY28 EPS of $198, or ~5x an EPS of ~$100. The market would be pricing FY28 earnings roughly halving: a DRAM/HBM contract-price turn well before the 2028 capacity, SCA renegotiation or an AI capex cut. That contradicts the SCA floors and 'no line of sight to balance' [2], so it would most likely mean a real cycle turn. Ordinary noise at 65-80% vol takes the stock 20-25% lower (~$820-860), not to $660. Moved from $700 because the corrected cash ($170 vs $120/sh) adds support under the price.

reasoning: Round 2. Accepted supervisor corrections: (1) my horizon net cash of ~$120/sh wrongly deducted buybacks while keeping 1.13B shares; rebuilt at ~$170/sh on 1.15B diluted shares ($55.6B ex-deposits + ~$150B FY27 FCF); (2) 5.5x was a ~17% premium to the clean NTM core median of ~4.7x; I now use 5.1x (~8%), dropping the net-cash argument because Samsung has large net cash too; (3) peer set pruned to the five DRAM/NAND makers, EV/EBITDA restated on NTM; (4) FY28 haircut narrowed from 5% to 4% ($198) since consensus is more likely to rise. Lane follow-ups (6 queries): no strike-vote result yet as of 5 Oct; Micron's revised bonus framework awaits board approval in early Oct [19]; spot data show a plateau (DDR4 1Gx8 +0.55% w/w, DDR4 2Gx8 correcting, NAND wafer -1% w/w, 'no clear buying interest' [16]; DDR5 +3.7% 30d, DDR4 16Gb 'early cooling' [4]). Spot leading contract is the classic early-turn signal, so I nudged the bear probability up (25% to 27%) and the bull down (25% to 23%). Fair value: P/E $1,010 and normalized+cash $1,196, blend $1,103 (+2.6%), vs round 1 $1,119. Disagreement with supervisor: it reconciles ~$1,020; I stay higher because I weight a normalized-earnings method that credits the SCA floor and the corrected cash, which a peak-P/E method ignores. Ladder: lognormal mixture (bear 600/27%/sigma 0.33, base 1,110/50%/0.22, bull 1,680/23%/0.24), tails slightly fattened; median ~$1,080, P(>=1075) 0.515 (was 0.56), answering the supervisor's point that my centre above spot was not warranted by a FV only ~4% above. Thesis break rebuilt at $660. One month: no print, strike headlines and spot plateau give a small negative tilt; P(>=spot) 0.465. Reddit and X still not fetchable.
